intro: Step inside Erzurum Museum, a museum in Erzurum province, opened in 1967. Here the Early Bronze Age and Urartian finds of eastern Anatolia are gathered together, with the black burnished pottery of the Karaz culture at their heart.
history: Opened in 1967, the museum gathers the Early Bronze Age cultures of eastern Anatolia. At its core is the black burnished pottery tradition named after the Karaz mound near Erzurum — a tradition that spread across a wide belt from the Caucasus to Iran.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Karaz culture pottery, the Urartian works, the Seljuk section and the ethnography hall.
facts: Did you know? Karaz pottery was built by hand rather than thrown, then burnished with a pebble after firing. That is why it still shines like a mirror thousands of years on. The same pottery appears across a belt from the Caucasus to Iran, pointing to a wide network of movement in the Early Bronze Age.
outro: This brings our tour of Erzurum Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. Thank you for spending this time with the makers of these pots. Enjoy your visit.
